Call MACS2 peaks for explicitly selected capture groups

Source: R/CallATACPeaks.R
CallATACPeaks.Rd

Split selected cells with Signac, run the installed MACS2 executable, and retain separate peak sets, command arguments and logs. Peak inference is performed by MACS2; no caller is installed or silently substituted.

Usage

CallATACPeaks(
  object,
  sample.by,
  group.by = NULL,
  cells = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  macs2.path = "macs2",
  outdir,
  effective.genome.size,
  qvalue = 0.05,
  extsize = 200L,
  shift = -extsize/2,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A validated Seurat object containing a ChromatinAssay and local indexed fragments with explicit cell mappings.

sample.by

Metadata column identifying capture/library IDs.

group.by

Optional metadata column subdividing each capture, for example a cell type. Calls are capture-by-group, never pooled across captures.

cells

Explicit selected assay cell IDs, or NULL for all assay cells.

assay

Source ChromatinAssay; NULL selects the active assay.

macs2.path

Path or PATH command name of an installed MACS2 2.x executable in the current runtime. On Windows use a prepared Linux container with explicit mounted paths. This function does not manage containers or translate host paths.

outdir

New output directory. Existing paths are rejected. Split BEDs, MACS2 outputs and logs remain here, including when a call fails.

effective.genome.size

Explicit effective genome size passed to MACS2.

qvalue

MACS2 q-value cutoff, strictly between zero and one.

extsize, shift

MACS2 fragment extension size and shift. The supported path uses BED input and --nomodel; MACS3 FRAG arguments are not used.

verbose

Whether Signac reports fragment splitting progress.

Value

A list with named peaks (GRanges per call), groups with columns call_id, sample and optional group, and receipt containing actual cell membership, reference, fragment resources, dependency versions, command arguments, logs, exit status and output files. The receipt identifies the original sample.by and group.by metadata fields; their names cannot collide with the fixed output columns. Counts represent the supplied fragment records, not fifth-column read-support weights. Peak significance is a caller result, not a biological-replicate condition comparison.

Details

Missing input, nonzero caller exit, missing output and malformed output are errors. A successful zero-byte narrowPeak file is a valid empty peak set; this is distinct from a failed call. No matrix or existing result is changed. receipt.rds and groups.rds are written before splitting/calling, and commands.rds plus the final receipt.rds are persisted once when the function exits (including on error). These retain selected cells, capture/group membership and resources for diagnosing failed calls. Combine the returned sets with CombineATACPeaks() and recount the resulting ranges with RecountATAC() before comparing previously different universes. Signac's splitting API is reused. The process is invoked directly so its exit status and both output streams can be retained, rather than relying on a caller wrapper that ignores the process exit status.

See also

RunATACQC(), CombineATACPeaks(), RecountATAC()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
called <- CallATACPeaks(atac,
  sample.by = "capture", group.by = "celltype",
  macs2.path = "/usr/local/bin/macs2", outdir = "atac_peak_calls",
  effective.genome.size = 2.7e9
)
common <- CombineATACPeaks(called$peaks, genome = "hg38")
} # }
